value: Never run bd init on a checkout: it rewrites CLAUDE.md and .claude/settings.json and commits them. A fresh clone or a cloud container uses bd bootstrap (session-start.sh does), then scripts/bd-sync.sh import.

bd update --notes REPLACES an issue's notes (it warns after the fact); add to them with --append-notes. Also: 'mise run deny msrv hack semver' passes the extra names to deny as arguments and fails; run the four tasks one by one.

target/ is a symlink into mbx's store, whose artifacts are read-only hard links: plain cargo cannot rebuild into it (output file ... is not writeable). Run cargo through mise exec, which applies the mbx wrapper from mise.toml; the git hooks use scripts/cargo-via-mise.sh.

In a cloud container api.github.com answers only for this repository, so mise's github, aqua and core backends cannot list versions: mise.cloud.toml (MISE_ENV=cloud) supplies the same tools from pinned release URLs, the cargo: tools too (built from crates.io they cost a fresh container twelve minutes; disable_tools names the cargo: entry, an http: entry replaces it). A version bump in mise.toml is a bump of the version and the URL there too.

A linker signal 7 (Bus error) is the session's disk allowance, not the code. Ollama models (about 10 GB for clef-flash) count against it, and the mbx ceiling in session-start.sh does not cover them: remove unused models first.

A new document under examples/jud/ or a new directory under examples/recordings/ moves the counts in tests/jud.rs and tests/contract.rs and needs a request snapshot; update them together, since one count at a time cost two failed pushes.

mise run check used to fail 3 jud_loop tests: docs:check (gen-cli-reference.sh, jud:check) rebuilds target/debug/jud with --features cli only while test runs it. Fixed by wait_for test on docs:check (judgment-7zb). Any new task that builds jud with fewer features and can run beside test needs the same.

mise run hack runs cargo-hack --no-dev-deps, which rewrites Cargo.toml and restores its own backup at exit: never edit Cargo.toml (or let a failed disk write hit it) while it runs, and a pkill of one 'mise run X' inside a for-loop of gates leaves the loop running: kill the loop's shell. Disk: the mbx target (/root/.cache/mbx/targets) grows past 15 GiB across feature sets and mbx gc does not shrink it; 'mise exec -- mbx clean' does, but only with no cargo running; rm -rf /root/.cache/mbx/incremental frees ~5 GiB safely.

After a hand-resolved merge, diff .beads/issues.jsonl against origin/main before pushing: beads' pre-commit flush once exported the database over the merged file and took seven issues back. The pre-commit import now prevents it; the diff still proves it.

docs/llms-full.txt carries every page in the mkdocs nav, docs/project pages included, unless its frontmatter sets llms: false (scripts/gen-llms-txt.sh opted_out; no page does). A page's body change moves llms-full.txt; a description change moves llms.txt too. Regenerate with scripts/gen-llms-txt.sh after any script that rewrites a page (gen-cli-reference.sh), since the edit hook ran before it.

After a pull that adds a tool to mise.toml, the next mise exec or mise run compiles it first (cargo-semver-checks takes over ten minutes); inside a pre-push hook five at once failed the push with Not a directory. Run mise install right after the pull; the post-merge hook names what is missing.
On a CPU-only Ollama on a CPU with AMX, clef-flash aborts until libggml-cpu-sapphirerapids.so is moved aside; the Ollama version does not matter.

Ollaya in a cloud container: its install script needs zstd (apt-get install -y zstd; root is available), glibc 2.38+ (Ubuntu 24.04 has 2.39); install with OLLAYA_VERSION=x OLLAYA_NO_SERVICE=1 OLLAYA_INSTALL_DIR=$HOME/.local sh install.sh, run 'ollaya serve' in the background, 'ollaya pull laya:en' (814 MB, CPU, 21 s first load). A second instance for the bearer test: OLLAYA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11436 OLLAYA_API_KEY=... ollaya serve. github.com release pages answer 403 here but release downloads work.

A pull request with no checks after a push is a merge conflict: GitHub runs no pull-request workflow on an unmergeable merge. mergeable_state dirty confirms it; bring main in with a merge commit (the steward skill).
When pushing in the background, keep the whole log in the scratchpad, not a tail: the pre-push hook's first error line is the one that explains the failure, and a tail of three lines once hid it.
cargo test --test jud alone fails on required-features: pass the features the test target declares (or --all-features).
